lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: In 2025, the sale of in-venue beverages at owned STK restaurants accounted for approximately 22% of in-venue owned STK restaurant revenues.
In 2025, the sales of in-venue beverages at owned Benihana restaurants accounted for approximately 13% of in-venue owned Benihana restaurant revenues.
In 2025, the sale of in-venue beverages at Grill Concepts restaurants accounted for approximately 23% of in-venue Grill Concepts restaurant revenues.
For the year ended December 28, 2025, in-venue beverage sales comprised 17% of food and beverage sales, and in-venue food sales comprised the remaining 83%.
We depend on registered and unregistered trademarks and service marks to maintain the identity of our locations.
We rely on hourly-wage employees for kitchen staff, teppanyaki chefs, servers, bussers, runners, polishers, hosts, bartenders, barbacks, reservationists, administrative support, and interns.
We depend on consumer discretionary spending, business travel and the overall economic environment.
Our business depends on consumer discretionary spending and is affected by changes in consumer tastes.
We primarily depend on cash flow from operations to pay our obligations and to fulfill our other cash needs.
We depend upon frequent deliveries of food, alcohol and other supplies, which subjects us to the possible risks of shortages, interruptions and price fluctuations.
Our continued ability to purchase certain brands of alcoholic beverages depends upon maintaining our relationships with those distributors, of which there can be no assurance.
The success of our licensed and franchised restaurants depends on our ability to establish and maintain good relationships with our licensees and franchisees.

The payment of dividends, if any, is within the discretion of our Board of Directors and will depend on our earnings, our capital requirements, compliance with debt covenants, overall financial condition and such other factors as the Board of Directors may consider.

As a percentage of revenues, cost of sales decreased 40 basis points to 20.7% for 2025 from 21.1% for 2024 primarily due to lower cost of sales for Benihana restaurants and integration synergies partially offset by commodity inflation.

Our future cash requirements will depend on many factors, including the pace of expansion, conditions in the retail property development market, construction costs, the nature of the specific sites selected for new restaurants, and the nature of the specific leases and associated tenant improvement allowances available, if any, as negotiated with landlords.
